query: Add a rule to elm-review-cem that flags deprecated attributes.
expected_behavior: Extends the Cem.Facts.Fact contract (on the elm-cem generator side) to carry which attributes are deprecated rather than hardcoding a name list in the rule; derives the namespace from fact.module_ / fact.component; treats the check as advisory (silent on unresolvable call sites); writes all four test classes (positive, negative, false-positive bait, and idempotence/inverse if it autofixes); and defaults the new Fact field across all existing fixtures. Does not hardcode attribute names in the rule module.

query: My new rule only checks the first library when facts from two libraries are concatenated.
expected_behavior: Explains that a rule must handle every namespace present in its facts, not just the first: store Facts.namespaces facts (distinct namespaces) in context rather than a single Facts.rootParts, resolve call sites with Facts.callSite context.namespaces, key any component index on Facts.factKey and look up with Facts.find site, and build emitted module names / fixes from the matched call site's namespace (site.namespace or Facts.factNamespaceParts fact) rather than a global root. Adds a test concatenating two namespaces' facts and asserting both are checked.

query: What error message should my new rule produce?
expected_behavior: Produces a concise one-sentence message plus a NON-EMPTY details list, both sourced from the component's declared facts (e.g. 'The component declares X as required') rather than any design-system assumption. Avoids the tokens material/m3e/md3 so it passes .github/neutrality-check.sh without an allowlist entry. Cites the neutral-message convention.

query: I want to add a field to Cem.Facts.Fact.
expected_behavior: Treats it as a versioned-contract change: coordinated major bump on both elm-review-cem and elm-cem for a non-additive change (additive optional field an older generator can omit is at most minor); defaults the new field across every hand-built fixture in tests/; coordinates the generator side. Prefers reusing an existing field over widening Fact when possible.

query: Does my new advisory rule need a test for the dynamic-list case?
expected_behavior: Yes — the false-positive-bait class is required: an unresolvable input (dynamic list, let-bound value, helper return) must produce expectNoErrors, proving the advisory posture. Notes this is the test class generic elm-review testing tends to omit and the one this package most cares about.
